name: golang-skills
description: 24 modular skills for idiomatic Go 1.27 — each under 400 lines, backed by 68 reference files, 10 automation scripts (--json on all ten, --limit where output is unbounded, --force on the three that write files), and 5 asset templates. Covers HTTP servers and clients, database/sql access, trust-boundary security, retries and idempotency, overload and failure containment, root-cause troubleshooting, behavior-preserving refactoring of existing code, generic methods, errors.AsType, synctest, the go fix modernizers, the stdlib-first dependency ladder, plus error handling, naming, testing, concurrency, interfaces, generics, documentation, logging, and performance. One shared verification gate (vet, test -race, go fix, lint, govulncheck) defines done, and the bundled golangci-lint baseline enforces the skills' rules. Ships a go-verify subagent, a PostToolUse gofmt/vet/go fix hook, a routing gate that holds the first Go edit until go-code has loaded the owner skills, a UserPromptSubmit hook that names go-code or go-code-refactor when a prompt asks for Go work, and a SubagentStart hook that repeats that note to every subagent started in a Go project. Activates automatically with progressive disclosure and conditional cross-references.
